what: Generative UI means the model builds the interface on the fly - but safely: it chooses from a catalog of known components and fills their props through typed, schema-checked actions, instead of writing raw HTML or code into your page.
like: Like a teacher with a box of magnetic shapes, labels and diagrams for the whiteboard: endless combinations, but every piece is one you made and tested.
why: The tutor can show a graph, a 3D model or a concept map exactly when it helps
Every action is validated, so bad output can't break or attack the page
Actions stream one by one, so the board builds up while the tutor speaks

steps.d: Instead of text, the model emits tool calls like draw, showGraph or offerOptions with arguments.
Each action type has a Zod schema; anything that doesn't parse is rejected and the model is asked again.
Props fill components from your catalog (3D scene, graph, formula, concept map, option cards), so the look stays on-brand and accessible.
A sanitiser fixes unknown ids and normalises coordinates; tldraw's agent kit applies each action as soon as it finishes streaming.
When a mini-simulation must be generated, it runs in a sandboxed iframe with no network, never in the page itself.
Every applied action lands in the event log for replay, grading evidence and evals.

numbers.l: tldraw starter kits: Agent, Chat, Branching chat, Workflow

choices.d: A catalog is safe, testable and consistent; free-form code is flexible but must be sandboxed and is hard to evaluate. Use code only for the rare simulation.
Small actions (create, update, move) stream nicely and are easy to validate; huge 'render this page' actions arrive late and fail as a whole.
tldraw's agent gets a screenshot, simplified shape data, the selection and recent actions - enough context without the full document.

instead.why: The same mechanism without a UI: actions that call APIs
When the model must run real code, isolate it completely

breaks.d: It calls a shape the catalog doesn't have.
breaks.fix: Schemas list allowed types; the error goes back to the model to retry

breaks.see: Shapes overlap or move after placement
breaks.fix: Layout rules in the sanitiser; anchor new shapes to existing ones

breaks.d: Raw HTML from the model rendered in the page.
breaks.see: Script in the DOM from model output
breaks.fix: Never render raw HTML; generated code only in a sandboxed iframe

say: The tutor never writes HTML: it emits typed canvas actions validated by schemas, placing components from our catalog.
Actions stream and apply one by one, so the board builds while the tutor talks, and every action lands in the event log.
Generated simulations, the one exception, run in a sandboxed iframe with no network.

followups.q: How do you evaluate generative UI?
followups.a: Schema-validity rate, layout checks (overlap, off-screen), and rubric scores from screenshots, run on a fixed set of lesson prompts.

followups.q: Why not let the model write React?
followups.a: It's slow to stream, hard to validate, and a security risk in your page. A catalog gives 90% of the value safely.

today: Canvas SDKs ship agent kits built on this pattern: tldraw's agent starter kit validates each action with a schema, sanitises it, and applies it as it streams.

check.q: The safest way for an AI tutor to draw on the canvas?
check.a: Typed actions on a fixed component catalog, validated by schemas
d: Model writes raw HTML into the page
Model edits the DOM with JavaScript
check.why: Schemas and a catalog keep output safe, consistent and testable.

check.q: Where should generated simulation code run?
check.a: In a sandboxed iframe with no network
check.why: Isolation stops generated code touching the app or data.
